chunks: Three narrators - My father (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah said: Ahmad ibn Hilal narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Salih, from Isa ibn Abd Allah who is from the children of Umar ibn Ali, from his forefathers, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) who said: Allah, Mighty be His Glory, said to Musa (peace be upon him): 'O Musa! If the heavens and their inhabitants, and the seven earths, were in one scale, and "There is no god but Allah" were in the other scale, then "There is no god but Allah" would tip the scale.'

key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god but Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the weight of saying 'There is no god but Allah' compared to the entire universe?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, this hadith qudsi emphasizes the metaphysical weight of *Tawhid* by comparing the declaration 'La ilaha illa Allah' against the totality of the heavens and seven earths, illustrating that divine unity outweighs all creation. This narrative underscores the Shia scholarly view that monotheism is not merely a verbal affirmation but the fundamental axis of cosmic balance and spiritual merit.
